comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Landed across 9956f00 (the transport), 386c9e0 (config, regions, the bridge) and b4acea8 (the Linux corpus tier).

The transport question this card left open is answered: the control plane rides a forwarded unix socket, so the adapter is unchanged and a remote daemon is a socket path like any other. The data plane cannot - herdr publishes frames through a CLI over stdio - so a pane's bridge runs that command over the same ssh master, which also keeps a remote pane as cheap as a local one. CLI-over-ssh for everything was rejected on the per-intent connect cost; reimplementing the frame stream was rejected because it is bincode over herdr's internal types with no published schema.

Proven by ./dev --ssh against the real container: a snapshot over the forwarded socket, a command over the master, and 0 differences across all 11 recorded scenarios between the Linux daemon and the macOS one.

creator: Alexander Terp
description: Attach the devenv container's daemon alongside the local one - the mixed local/remote view herdr itself cannot do (their discussion #2232). Decide transport here: tunneled socket vs CLI-over-ssh.
title: Stage 2: second daemon over SSH in the same window
